# Washing Machine

## Setup

I plumbed the inlet hoses with the mesh washers seated properly and hand tightened the unions a quarter turn past snug. The drain hose hooks over the standpipe at about 65 cm so it cannot siphon back. I levelled the feet with a spirit level across the top, then locked the nuts. Cold fill is fine for most things here, so the hot tap stays closed. I set the default program to a 40 C cotton wash with an extra rinse, since the water here is hard.

## Cleaning

Once a month I run a 90 C drum clean cycle with a cup of soda crystals in the drum and nothing else. That lifts the residue film that builds from too much detergent and low temperature washes. Between cycles I wipe the door seal with a dilute vinegar cloth and leave the door ajar so it dries out. The detergent drawer pulls free for a scrub when it looks chalky.

## Maintenance

The drain pump filter sits behind the kick plate, and I clean it quarterly, pulling out coins, hair grips and the odd sock fragment. The detergent drawer comes out for a soak every few months. I check the inlet mesh filters once a year and clear any grit. The belt was replaced at the five year mark after it started slipping on heavy spins.

## Troubleshooting

A banging noise on spin usually means an unbalanced load, so I pause it and redistribute the items. Water left in the drum after a cycle points at a blocked pump filter or a kinked drain. An error code on the panel often clears if I power the unit down for a minute and restart. If the drum will not turn but the motor hums, the belt has likely come off its pulley.
